items.title: Nursing the Revolution
items.summary: Part of America 250 at Penn programming, this exhibit explores the overlooked yet essential role of nurses during the American Revolution, whose vital work helped shape early American healthcare. It challenges the widespread belief that nursing began in the 19th century with Florence Nightingale by providing rare evidence of a world of nursing and caretaking that thrived before, during, and after the American Revolution. Free and open to the Penn community.
items.image_alt: Front steps of Penn Nursing’s Fagin Hall in daylight

items.title: Allison Zuckerman: Remixed and Reclaimed
items.summary: This exhibition, on view in the Annenberg Center lobby and curated by the Arthur Ross Gallery inaugural faculty director Gwendolyn DuBois Shaw, will present a selection of recent paintings by Penn alum Allison Zuckerman that exemplify her exuberant, layered approach to image-making. Using paint and collage, Zuckerman creates densely constructed compositions that draw from art history, popular culture, and the internet. Her paintings celebrate the history of the image-making medium while reimagining who has the power to shape its future. Free and open to the public.
items.image_alt: Allison Zuckerman, Conferring with Grace, 2021. Acrylic, oil, rhinestones, and archival CMYK ink on canvas. A surrealist, vibrantly colorful artwork featuring various animal species, including a leopard, monkey, rabbit, and butterflies.
items.location: Annenberg Center for the Performing Arts, 3680 Walnut St.

items.title: Print the Declaration of Independence
items.summary: Participants of all ages and backgrounds are invited to this Common Press workshop to print a copy of the Declaration of Independence. The composition will be set in Caslon metal type and ready to print on the studio’s 1889 cast-iron handpress. These hour-long demonstrations are part of America 250 at Penn programming. Groups of up to 20 people are welcome. Reserve a time slot.
items.image_alt: A copy of the Declaration of Independence in the Common Press office.
items.location: Fisher Fine Arts Library, 220 S. 34th St.

items.title: Gifts of the Longhouse
items.summary: As Philadelphia commemorates the 250th anniversary of the nation’s founding, this Public Trust event invites audiences to reconsider the origins of American democratic thought by centering the governance traditions of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy (often referred to historically as the Iroquois Confederacy). The program will examine how its sophisticated systems of governance, diplomacy, consensus-building, and shared power—developed centuries before European contact—were encountered and studied by colonial leaders, including the influence on early American political thought and the U.S. Constitution. Free and open to the public. Register to attend.

items.title: Election Roundtable: Results, Analysis and What Comes Next
items.summary: Part of Penn Arts & Sciences’ long-running Knowledge by the Slice lunchtime series, this special post-election roundtable with political science faculty examining the results of the 2026 midterm elections, the broader state of elections in the U.S., and what the outcomes mean for the future of American politics. The discussion will explore key election results, emerging political trends, and what comes next. Free and open to the Penn community.
items.image_alt: A roll of "I voted!" stickers with a Penn logo sits on top colored fliers on a table

items.title: Life in the City of Brotherly Love During the Early Republic
items.summary: Inaugural faculty director of the Arthur Ross Gallery Gwendolyn DuBois Shaw and director of the Penn Art Collection Lynn Smith Dolby will lead a virtual tour of the Gallery’s fall exhibition, “At Liberty: Life in the City of Brotherly Love During the Early Republic.” The tour will be followed by a Q&A. Free and open to the public. Register to attend.
items.image_alt: The painting “Nightlife in Philadelphiaan Oyster Barrow in Front of the Chestnut Street Theater,” depicting people eating oysters on the street in Philadelphia in the 18th century.

items.title: Symposium: Stranger Things
items.summary: Co-organized by Elly R. Truitt, the Janice and Julian Bers Professor of the History of Science at Penn, the 19th annual Lawrence J. Schoenberg Symposium on Manuscript Studies in the Digital Age topic will interrogate the multiangled intersections of magic, science, religion, and ritual in the pre- and early modern world. Participants will explore the testimony of handwritten evidence to the ways in which the distinctions between science, magic, and religion were made, blurred, and interpreted for their readers and users. Free and open to the public. Register to attend.
items.image_alt: Hand paintings in an ancient text.

items.title: AI in Finance Lab Info Session
items.summary: The Wharton AI in Finance Lab brings together faculty and Ph.D. fellows who use large language models, machine learning, and new data to study questions in asset pricing, corporate finance, and innovation. At this information session, the Lab’s fellows will share the projects they are pursuing, the skills most valuable for research roles, and how to get involved. Undergraduate and master’s students with an interest in finance, coding, or AI are encouraged to attend. Free and open to the Penn community. Space is limited. Registration does not guarantee a seat.
items.image_alt: A hand holding a crystal ball with finance charts and graphs inside.

items.title: The Practice of Articulation
items.summary: Rachel Kolb, author of the recent memoir “Articulate: A Deaf Memoir of Voice,” will recount stories from a life spent practicing various types of articulation, both in English and in American Sign Language (ASL). Drawing from lived experiences and the process of writing her book, Kolb will discuss deafness as a source of insight that can deepen our analysis of the stakes of human connection, as well as illuminate more equitable and flexible ways of shaping our relationships with others. The talk will be followed by a Q&A and book signing. Free and open to the public.

items.title: Children Reinventing Cinema
items.summary: Curated by film and media scholar Wanda Strauven, this screening program will feature a series of short contemporary and historical films made by and/or alongside kids. The screening will be followed by a conversation between Strauven and Turkish visual artist Aslı Baykal, filmmaker of Darkroom (2023), moderated by Ann Wang, a Ph.D. student in Cinema & Media Studies at Penn. Free and open to the public. Register to attend.

items.title: Homecoming Weekend 2026
items.summary: Penn Alumni and their partners across the University welcome everyone back to campus for three days of programming during Homecoming Weekend. Registration is required for some events.
items.image_alt: alumni hold Penn '99 signs and umbrella for Alumni Parade

items.title: The Future of Community-Based Primary Care
items.summary: During Homecoming 2026, Penn Nursing will bring together leading medical experts and Penn alumni for “Practicing Where It Matters Most: The Future of Community-Based Primary Care,” the Inaugural Leonard A. Lauder Community Care Nurse Practitioner Program Symposium. All members of the Penn community are welcome. Participants are invited to attend the full-day symposium or register for the morning or afternoon session.
items.image_alt: A heart, paper cut out of four people, and a stethoscope.

items.title: Processing the U.S. Midterm Elections
items.summary: This program, organized by SNF Paideia, brings together visiting students from the United States Studies Centre at the University of Sydney and students from across Penn for a conversation about the U.S. midterm elections. Participants will hear reflections from students in Penn’s Political Empathy Lab; Program on Opinion Research and Election Studies; Penn Leads the Vote; and Penn political science professor Matthew Levendusky, followed by small group discussions. Refreshments will be served. Free and open to the Penn community.
items.image_alt: Open desks at a polling station.

items.title: Arts at Penn Launch Party
items.summary: This launch party will celebrate the essential role the arts have always played at Penn. Vice provost for the arts Timothy Rommen will share plans for advancing the arts at the University. Then, Institute of Contemporary Art director Johanna Burton will invite participants to experience a unique tour created by theatre arts director Brooke O’Harra and student ambassadors. Provost John L. Jackson, Jr. will lead a toast to kick off the reception and mid-day dance party with a DJ set by second-year Sarah Parmet. The first 100 attendees will receive limited edition Arts at Penn swag. Free and open to the public. Register to attend.
items.location: Institute of Contemporary Art, 118 S. 36th St.
